title: Paid extra for “luxury”  still had to pay for heating
text:
We were satisfied with the general organization of the Sahara trip, but what happened with transport and the “luxury” desert camp was completely unacceptable.
We traveled in February, when mornings and nights are very cold. The van used for transport had no heating at all. It was freezing inside, and we had to sit in winter jackets for hours every morning until the sun warmed the van from outside. My legs were literally freezing after those rides. This is basic comfort and safety, and it should be guaranteed.
The biggest disappointment was the so-called “luxury” desert accommodation, for which we paid an extra about €50 per person. There was no heating in the tent. When we told reception that the AC/heating was not working, they told us: “You are traveling with this agency, and your package does not include AC.”
So we were forced to pay an extra €40 just to have heating during the night.
This is not “luxury.” This is misleading and dishonest. If you sell a luxury desert tent in February, heating should absolutely be included in the price — not charged as an extra after arrival. That feels like a scam, and it is embarrassing for both the agency and the camp.
If you book this trip, make sure you ask in writing exactly what is included, because the advertised “luxury” option may not be what you think.

title: It is worth what you pay for, nothing
text:
I signed up what the city posters scream is a free tour. We were 5, Barcelona, Gaudí, towers scraping the sky like they’re trying to escape us. It all sounded beautiful enough.

We show up. First thing they do is ask for 1.5€ for an audio dongle (some small plastic parasite meant to whisper facts into your ear). Not free anymore, not even close. I refused the gadget, because someone around here has to uphold the meaning of the word “free,” but my friends caved, like people usually do when a price is small enough not to make noise in their conscience.

The guide, whose name “Marcos?”, “Martin?”, my mind refused to archive after what came next, was cultured, sure. Spanish history spilling out of him like wine from a cracked bottle. Argentinian roots, maybe even a poet in a past life, before he turned into a watchdog for a company that seems to train its people in the art of soft extortion.

The tour began at 10:30.
We stood still until 11.
Thirty minutes of verbal drizzle, all ramble and no rain.

In three hours, we moved maybe four streets! A pilgrimage of microscopic proportions. Not a tour, but a hostage situation with trivia.

And then came the great collection of the sacred audio dongles. We returned four, because I never took one. That’s when the man snapped, like a bad character in an even worse novel. He barked about protocols, rules, that it was “not allowed” to do the tour without the dongle. Imagine that: a free tour where you need to pay for the equipment you don’t want, led by a guide who looks at you like you’ve personally insulted his ancestors by refusing.

He ranted, he shouted, 20€ tips per person, demanded like tithes for a church nobody believes in. Public humiliation dressed up as customer service. My friends heard it, the street heard it, maybe even Gaudí himself rolled in his grave out of second hand embarrassment.

I didn’t fight back.
Some arguments smell too bad to touch.
I turned my back and walked away, letting his words rot in the air behind me.

This company seems to hire its guides by throwing darts at a map and hoping whoever it hits can yell loud enough. No background checks, no dignity, no understanding of what free means. A masterpiece of false advertising and forced generosity, where you’re guilttripped into tipping for a tour that barely moved.

A flawless demonstration of free will:
I freely booked a free tour that wasn’t free,
was freely yelled at,
and freely reminded why some things are worth exactly what you pay for!
and sometimes even less.

title: These people are crooks
text:
These people are crooks.  I booked them for their "best selling" Pristine Sistine tour.  Their website contains blatant lies and false advertising, which you don't realize until you are actually on the tour.

This is what their website says: "Enter the Sistine Chapel just as it opens, ahead of the daytime tour groups."

This is a lie.  You have to wake up early and overpay (I paid $200) for NOTHING.  It is only when you arrive that the guide tells you that the Vatican changed their rules years ago, and you do not enter the Sistine Chapel as it opens, and in fact it is not even the first stop on the tour.  When we arrived at the Vatican, we waited to the side as other groups went in first, and then our guide proceeded slowly and babbled and it was clear that we would not enter the Sistine Chapel until around 10 am.

You can see how badly this company rips you off when you look at the €25 museum admission ticket.  You are basically paying $200 for a ticket that costs $28, with zero added value.

I joined this tour with my partner so it was $400 wasted.  The guide was also terrible, a complete amateur, and kept repeating himself.  He began rushing us through, only to stop at random exhibits and babble for 5 minutes, offering nothing of value.  I became alarmed when I looked at a museum sign next to one of the exhibits and it was far more insightful than our babbling guide.

This tour was so bad that my partner and I left after around 90 minutes in.  We proceeded to purchase the €5 official audio guide, sold by the Vatican, and it was infinitely better than our babbling guide.  I would have disputed the charge on my credit card for the blatant false advertising that Walks of Italy engages in, clear lies on their website, but unfortunately it was too late for me to dispute it.  As this company is run by crooks, I know there is no chance I will get a refund from them.

All I can do is caution others not to spend $200 on a $30 ticket and guide, so others don't get robbed by these crooks like I was.

I was asked for my contact information and told that management would contact me directly.  They never did, and instead left a response here with fake concern, pretending they would like more information from me.

I then contacted the company again.  I was told that management was in the process of conducting an "investigation" and would reach out to me next week.  This was over 10 days ago.  It is clear they are crooks and just making fake responses here to look like a respectable company.  Would never use them again.  BTW, their false and deceptive language is still on their website.

title: One star only because I can’t give…
text:
One star only because I can’t give zero. Despite the name and description of the tour, this tour does not get you into the Vatican museums before opening. Once meeting with your guide, you will walk to the group tour line outside the museum entrance and will stand there until opening at 8. Once going through security, our guide immediately let the whole group go on a 15 minute bathroom break which seemed quite unnecessary and a waste of time at the beginning of the tour. Once the tour actually started (close to 8:30), many groups and individuals had gone ahead into the museums and there was already congestion forming. It felt as if our guide was purposely wasting time. For example, we spent quite a bit of time outside at the pine cone and at each exhibit. Again, our guide was taking so long at the initial exhibits that groups and individuals were easily passing us. My husband and I became so frustrated with the pacing of our tour guide that we turned in our headset and continued on ourselves. Looking back, I am quite glad we did this. title: Thank you for following up and asking…
text:
Thank you for following up and asking why we were dissatisfied with our experience. I am outlining the details below so there is no misunderstanding as to why this tour was unacceptable.

After spending approximately $1,000 USD on your Key Masters Vatican tour in 2024, my daughter and I had high expectations for your Amalfi–Pompeii day trip in 2025. Visiting Amalfi was the primary reason we booked this tour. Because of its importance, we contacted your company every single day prior to departure to confirm that the itinerary would, in fact, include Amalfi. Each time, we were explicitly told by your representatives that we were going to Amalfi.

We intentionally selected Monday, June 16, 2025 to avoid weekend congestion and crowds. Despite this, our booking was changed without my consent to a Sorrento itinerary. I immediately called to have this corrected and was once again reassured that we were “for sure” going to Amalfi.

On the day of the tour, after visiting Pompeii, we were informed upon boarding the van that we would no longer be going to Amalfi due to a traffic jam and that it would “take all day” to clear. I checked Google Maps in real time and saw that the traffic issue cleared within approximately one hour. This explanation was inconsistent with the information available and directly contradicted the repeated confirmations we had received. At that point, the diversion to Sorrento felt misleading and inappropriate, given that we paid specifically for an Amalfi itinerary.

When I expressed our dissatisfaction and requested a refund—because we were promised Amalfi, paid for Amalfi, and relied on multiple confirmations that we were going there—our concerns were dismissed. We did not receive a refund, not even a partial one, despite the tour materially differing from what was sold to us.

This experience was extremely disappointing and reflects poor business practices. We spent a significant amount of money and did not receive the experience that was advertised or repeatedly confirmed. Compounding this frustration was the dismissive manner in which our concerns were handled when we raised them, including when we stated at the time that this situation was not acceptable.

At this point, unless this matter is properly addressed, we will be leaving detailed reviews on your website, Google, and TripAdvisor to warn other travelers of our experience. Given the amount of money spent, the lack of any refund, and the way our concerns were handled, we believe it is important for future customers to be fully informed.

We would still welcome a fair resolution, but the dissatisfaction stems directly from misrepresentation of the itinerary and the failure to address the issue appropriately once raised.

title: Disappointed by Inflexibility and Tone Around Accessibility
text:
We were very interested in joining the Deluxe Harry Potter Tour with City Wonders and contacted the company in advance to explain that our teenage son uses a wheelchair. Since the provided transportation was not accessible for him, we asked if we could meet the group directly at the studios. We were flexible, willing to arrive early, and ready to coordinate in any way necessary to avoid disruption to the group.

Unfortunately, the operator declined our request and the tone of the communication was, frankly, disappointing. In explaining their decision, they stated that the tour “would not be able to slow down or take extra breaks” for wheelchair users. This was upsetting to hear — not only because we hadn’t asked for any special pacing or accommodations, but because it assumed that our son would need those things. He wouldn’t. The assumption felt ableist and dismissive of his actual capabilities, and the unwillingness to engage in any kind of collaborative problem-solving was frustrating.

While we recognize that some logistical limitations may exist, service providers in the UK are expected under the Equality Act 2010 to make reasonable adjustments for disabled guests. We did not feel that obligation was taken seriously in this case.

This may be a wonderful tour for many, but travelers with accessibility needs should be aware that accommodations may not be offered — and that the company’s tone and approach to disability-related requests may leave you feeling excluded rather than welcomed.

title: DO NOT GIVE THESE PEOPLE YOUR MONEY
text:
DO NOT GIVE THESE PEOPLE YOUR MONEY - they ruined the first day of my trip and their customer service was that appalling it left me in tears. 

We booked the crypts and catacombs tour - which cost me over £90 for two of us and it really was supposed to be the highlight of my trip.

We arrived at the meeting point only to find they’d gone without us. I was gutted. Desperate to try and catch them up I went over to another tour group from a different company that were meeting at the same location to ask which direction ,y tour had gone in - only to be told that my group had a ctually left prior to the 5pm start time. 

This was then confirmed by some other tourists who were sat by the fountain when the tour had left.

The worst part about this was the rude customer service team. I explained the situation and that I had been told the tour left prior to the start time on the tickets, whilst they initially told me it wasn’t their problem they refused to tell me the location of the group so we could join and enjoy the 2.5hr tour.
We said we would get a can to the first location which would mean we would definitely arrive their before the group were due to but they said no they would not allow this (despite our entry to the crypts and catacombs being included in the tour price). They refused to give us the number of the person leading the tour (one customer service rep said it was a lady and the other rep said it was a man so shows how much they known about their own tours.) 

We were then offered a reschedule but would have to pay another £50 which I was more than willing to do they said their next available date was the 19th May (we are leaving Rome before so that wasn’t an option. I have later been back on their get your guide page and they had availability on the 13th but this wasn’t offered.

My father tried to speak to them and got no where at which point I was in floods of tears asking for at least a voucher I could use towards on of their other tours as I’ve saved for ages to do this trip. I have a masters in early Christian history so this was on my bucket list. I do not earn much money as I work for the emergency services and very rarely get an opportunity such as this. However, by this point they then became extremely dismissive and were gloating that it was my problem not theirs. The lady from customer service I was speaking to was then speaking to me in the most patronising way like I was a child which got frustrated and so finally I gave up and asked her for her name as I would hate for anyone else to have the experience that I did (unfortunately looking at recent reviews it seems that I am one of many to have this awful experience with this company) ultimately she flat out refused to give me her name saying she didn’t have too - this just goes to show that she clearly knew her handling of the situation did not meet the professional standards this company claims to have.

I will be formally requesting a refund, at least in part and will take it further if needs be but I feel they’ve robbed me of an amazing experience and wasted the first part of my trip which is something I won’t get back so I’d advise you think very carefully about using this company. 

They are not the only ones to offer this tour and there are many more reputable companies which offer the same but that are guest focused.

title: Normandy tour sites are amazing. Despite the tour guide just recommending WW2 movies the whole time instead of History
text:
We did a Normandy tour from Paris in November 2024. While the things we saw were amazing, and we were able to see multiple sites, I was not impressed by this tour.

I have been to many tours and completely understand the need for punctuality when visiting multiple sites. First the pick up point is confusing for tourists, and should be more clear. Unfortunately, The guide, Daniel, was not clear in his direction, and my group felt extremely rushed at every location. The guide constantly talked about movies and film instead of facts or history. Considering he was guiding a tour specific to Normandy battles, the audience is considerably more interested in things like “why was this village significant?”, “what was the people’s reception to the Allied forces here?”, but no. He spent the whole time talking about himself and giving plot details about Saving Private Ryan. 

We arrived at the American Cemetery at Omaha Beach, and he complained that other tours will only give you 30 minutes, but he would graciously give us an hour. But after a short but weaving story about the beach landing, and then him telling stories about himself, we only had 35 minutes to see the cemetery and visit the museum/visitor center. He did not give tips on what to see, or how to budget time, or what was in the museum. We speed ran the museum in 10 minutes after the flag ceremony and were late for the bus. Even though the museum was only open for 15 more minutes, we could not stay only to be done with our day. 

He then spent the rest of the bus ride home talking about other World War 2 movies instead of giving information or asking for questions. 

Perhaps other tours here are better, with other guides, but I’d be wary.

title: City Wonders? The Wonder is why anyone uses this exploitative company.
text:
I booked three events with City Wonders through Expedia, expecting a great experience for our time in Rome. 

On the first trip (A colosseum and palatine hill guided tour) we arrived on time, only to be told that our guide wasn't coming in that day.  We were instead provided with the two tickets and told we should go by ourselves, with a partial refund.

Our day had been planned around this event so we were left without much option.  

The tickets had a face value of 18.50 euros each, and our tour had cost 169 pounds (GBP), (or effectively 200 euros,) meaning that the majority cost was for the guide with the tour.

When we returned home, we found our partial refund was 50% of the overall cost i e. 84.50 GBP.  

With the tickets costing around 31 GBP converted, this meant that we were charged in excess of 50 GBP for the privilege of doing things ourselves. (More than 1 and a half times more than the cost of the tickets themselves.)

We challenged this refund with Expedia, but they said they could not help, and City Wonders backed up their insult by saying that the tour was non-refundable (in other words, suck it up).

If this had been reversed and we had not shown for the tour, the failing would have been ours, but the liberties from a company that has already tied your hands behind your back are unacceptable.

On top of this, the organisation for the other trips was  incredibly poor, bordering on manic.  The administration gets you to the venue on time, but the meeting point itself involved half a dozen people in blue shirts, trying to shout above the hustle and bustle of a busy tourist square, looking to coordinate around 10 tours at once.  

At least half those present were struggling to find where they should be, (questioning and complaining with each other) and when the question was raised to the individual who appeared to be the lead blue shirt, he was rude to the customers, arrogant, and clearly more concerned with how he looked in front of the female guests, than how he supported the customers.

City Wonders?  The real Wonder is how this company has managed to monopolise the area for so long.

That said, the guides on the tours were contractors to, not employees of City Wonders, and the ones that supported our other tours were very good.  Laura and Barbara were their names, and it was they that effectively saved our days, in what was otherwise a maelstrom of ineptitude.

City Wonders are merely coordinators, and not very good ones.  Our experience suggests that it is better to buy tours on the ground in Rome, where you can at least control your own approach.

We read reviews on City Wonders before we went with them, but our mistake was starting at the top and working down until we had seen enough.  I would recommend reading more reviews but start from the bottom.  

There are so many bad reviews that you will soon realise, the common denominator is not the customer here.

title: I would give 0 stars if possible.
text:
I went on 6/30/24 and it was an absolute disaster. To begin we get on the bus and they let us get 2 hours down the road before they tell us that the boat to Amalfi is not working. They said that the previous day there had been a strike with the boat workers. So they couldn’t convince me that they didn’t know we were going to run into issues the next day. They had this planned and were just hoping that we would accept their lackluster plan B of going to Sorrento. So the people on the bus complained and the guide Sonja said that she was going to try to get us at least on a boat to Postiano from Sorrento. So we get to Sorrento and we have a rushed lunch at a super expensive place (at least is was good). Then we meet back up only for Sonja to tell us that she could not even secure to boat to Postiano. Then she says we only have less than 2 hours in Sorrento. Sorrento doesn’t even have a free beach you have to wait in a long line and then pay 15-20 euros to even get to be able to go in the water. Which I did because I was not going to let my day be completely ruined. I only got to spend about 45 minutes in the water before rushing back up the hill to meet back up to go back to Rome. We spent 6-7 hours on the bus in heavy traffic (which I do recognize was not the tour companies fault). Then Sonja had no ability to read the room and was trying to get us to dance the YMCA on the way back with a bus full of angry people (not even lying… so bizarre) which just made me even more mad.

The other thing that was simply not ok was Sonja’s treatment of a Japanese lady on the bus who had trouble understanding. She maybe thought she was helping but she was downright aggressive with that poor woman. She kept offensively calling her Japonese and complaining to other people the woman couldn’t understand her. She then started yelling at her in Italian because she couldn’t understand. The lady was visibly upset to the point of crying. When we got to Sorrento Sonja grabbed the Japanese lady by the arm and led her and I can tell she was uncomfortable. The lady got off in Sorrento and I hope she was able to at least get on the boat like we were not able to. The treatment of that lady made me sick to my stomach honestly. I hope she is ok.

On the ride home along with the terrible YMCA incident Sonja kept telling us to not leave her a bad review because it wasn’t her fault about the boat. True. But your attitude toward everyone is your fault and it was awful. She was extremely rude to me when I asked her a question about a meetup spot. She obviously didn’t understand English very well which was a lie on City Wonders part that they had “expert guides who spoke English”.

The other thing was that I overheard some other passengers talking who had a brother who went to the coast because the boats were in fact working. So I think this was a huge scam to see if they could get away with it. I just thank the people who made a big fuss on the bus because I think that is the only reason we are getting our refunds processed (and thank you to the person who I saw recording every time they spoke on the bus). They should have told us in the morning it was not happening (because it was clear from the get go it wasn’t) and gave us our refunds so we could have had our day in Rome.

In all it was a long bus ride with a stop to a limoncello factory that no one even cared about and we got a small lemon soap as a consolation prize. Do not book this experience and if you do proceed with caution. You are better off catching the train and booking your own ferry ticket. And Sonja needs some training on how to deal with people if she is working in hospitality.

Also there is a place they let you get off for a “pit stop” that is literally highway robbery. 16 euros for a cheese and tomato sandwich, small bottle of water, and can of sprite. This is obviously just a huge cash grab so if you risk this experience then bring your own food unless you don’t care about overspending.

The only positive I will say is the bus driver did his best to get us back to Rome despite the traffic. But when we got back the subway lines were down and I had to pay for an expensive taxi back to my hotel.

This was a gut wrenching experience and the only reason I came to Italy was for Amalfi. I don’t know if and when I can come back but when I do I am going to just book my own stuff and not rely on any tour companies anymore. Citywonders should be ashamed. I hope anyone on that bus reading this was able to capitalize on their time in Rome and I am sorry for all of us about the major let down.

text:

title: VIATOR BUYER BEWARE
text:
VIATOR BUYER BEWARE - especially with City Wonders Tours!
I booked an early access tour for myself and my children to the Vatican, Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter's Basilica. We arrived PRIOR to the required meeting time so that we could find our tour group. However, NONE of our booking documents/tickets listed the name of the tour company. We approached EVERY SINGLE TOUR GUIDE asking if they could help. We showed each of them our tickets and booking documents and not a single one of them were able to help us because THEY couldn't even find who the tour company was supposed to be. I attempted to call the tour operator, as recommended on our bookings. When calling, I was immediately put on hold and then disconnected - TWICE! By this point we had missed the departure time (again, despite arriving well before the stated meeting time).  I then sent a message to the tour operator, according to the booking procedures. I stated the situation and requested a refund since there was nothing else I could have done to attempt to find out who we should have met with. As it turns out, the tour group was City Wonders. They responded to my email and basically told me that I was at fault for not being with the group at the required meeting time. But the question is, what else could I have done? I followed all of their procedures. I arrived earlier than the stated meeting time. I asked every tour guide and group to see if they were able to help me identify which tour company I was assigned to - INCLUDING A CITY WONDERS TOUR GUIDE (who was so lovely and really tried to help but even HE could not find the information!), showing each my ticket and booking information. NOBODY was able to help us identify the necessary information to meet our group. Also, according to their stated procedure, I phoned but was immediately put hold and then cut off TWICE! After all of this was unsuccessful, and after now wasting all of this time and missing the actual departure time, I sent an email message to the tour operator (City Wonders) about the situation. Their response? Basically, "So Sorry So Sad. You just should have known." I'm sorry, but that should not be acceptable. This was a situation out of my control, yet they and the booking company Viator, refuse to provide any support. It is incredibly disheartening to realize that people pay a significant amount of money for tours like this because they are often once-in-a-lifetime opportunities. But they and the booking company do not hold themselves to the same standards they hold their customers to. I never want anyone to go through this, follow all of their rules and guidelines, and basically be told to go f- off when they failed to provide the information that is ESSENTIAL to actually participating in the event! Please use caution if you use either Viator or City Wonders because you may be robbed of both your hard-earned money and meaningful experiences.

title: Our visit to Auschwitz-Birkenau was a great disappoinment
text:
Our visit to Auschwitz-Birkenau was supposed to be one of the most meaningful journeys of our lives. Instead, it became one of the most disappointing travel experiences we have ever had.
We booked our guided tour through GetYourGuide on March 23, 2025, more than a year in advance. This visit was deeply personal to us because my wife’s grandmother experienced the war herself, and her stories inspired us to visit Auschwitz-Birkenau with the respect and preparation such a place deserves.
We travelled all the way from the Netherlands and carefully planned this journey over the course of a year. On our way, we even visited war memorials in Leipzig to fully understand the historical significance of this trip. The emotional highlight of our journey was supposed to be Auschwitz-Birkenau on May 3, 2026.
Then, on the evening before the tour, we suddenly received an email stating that our guide had cancelled the tour. At first, we thought it was spam because it was so unbelievable. After confirmation, we learned that the cancellation was real — less than 24 hours before our visit.
Despite this shock, we still travelled from Ostrava to Oświęcim because we had already come so far. Upon arrival at Auschwitz-Birkenau, we discovered that we had no valid tickets because the guide supposedly had them. GetYourGuide told us the local operator was responsible. The local operator blamed the guide. The guide was unreachable for everyone.
What hurt the most was the complete lack of empathy and support. Nobody seemed to care that we had travelled from another country for this deeply emotional visit. No alternative solution was offered. Not even the possibility of joining another group was considered.
After waiting for over two hours outside the entrance, we had no choice but to leave and drive back disappointed.
Of course, our disappointment is nothing compared to the unimaginable suffering of the millions of people who lost their lives there. But precisely because this place carries such historical and emotional importance, the careless handling of our booking made the experience even more painful.
This experience seriously damaged our trust in GetYourGuide and the local organization they work with. We understand that cancellations can happen, but abandoning visitors without communication, support, empathy, or solutions is simply unacceptable.
Sadly, instead of sharing a meaningful experience with our family and friends afterward, we can only share how we were left standing outside the gates of Auschwitz-Birkenau after travelling across Europe for a visit that never happened.
— Fam. R. from the Netherlands

title: No Action Taken Over Inappropriate Conduct
text:
I booked 2 tickets for a Douro Valley wine tour through Tiqets with Living Tours Porto, and I am extremely disappointed with both the experience and how this has been handled.

The guide, Paolo, who introduced himself as “Slimmy,” was completely inappropriate with me throughout the trip. He was stroking my arms, grabbing and squeezing me, and repeatedly calling me “beautiful.” At first we put it down to over-friendliness, but it became very clear this was repeated, unwanted attention, especially as I was visibly cringing away.

He then asked me on a date and said we should get coffee (this man was visibly twice my age). I was stuck on a bus with him and felt so uncomfortable but told him no, I don't have time.

After that, he repeatedly pressured me to add him on Instagram. I told him I had no data. He told me to use the bus Wi-Fi. I then said my phone would not connect, and he still kept pushing and even tried to look at my phone. He did not do this to anyone else.

It got to the point that I had to pretend to sleep for the rest of the journey just so he would leave me alone, which meant missing the views and part of the experience I had paid for. My friend and others on the bus had to keep stepping in because it was so uncomfortable.

When we got off the bus, he singled me out again and tried to hug me, which he did not do with anyone else. I had to say no and offer a handshake instead, and even that I was uncomfortable with at that point. Afterwards, my friend looked at his Instagram and found that he is married and has a daughter close to my age, which made the whole situation even more unsettling.

This was not friendliness. It was creepy, intrusive, and unprofessional. I would not recommend this tour, and I would not feel comfortable recommending it to other women.

Also, the “cheese and olive oil tasting” was misleading and basically nonexistent. Its a shame because the views were gorgeous but honestly go with a different company.

I am extremely frustrated with how this has been handled by both Tiqets and Living Tours Porto. My complaint has effectively been dismissed because he has “so many good reviews.” That does not make this behaviour acceptable, and it does not mean it didn’t happen. I also offered witness accounts from other people who approached me during the tour to tell me they would vouch for me as they had witnessed his behaviour.

Just because someone has positive reviews does not mean they do not act like this towards women. If this were your daughter, your friend, or someone you care about, you would not want them put in this position on a tour.

Shame on Tiqets for hiding behind reviews instead of taking this seriously, and shame on Living Tours Porto for continuing to employ a guide who makes women feel this uncomfortable.

Very disappointing experience. I booked tickets for the Grand Sumo Tournament and received confirmation, only for them to be cancelled 4 weeks later—just over a week before the event.

These tickets are known to be hard to obtain, so this left me with limited options. It was also a 50th birthday gift for my husband, which made the situation even more frustrating.

A refund was issued, but cancelling confirmed bookings this close to the event is not acceptable.

title: Beware if you are delayed getting to…
text: Beware if you are delayed getting to the meeting point because they will not even wait 10 minutes, and will not give you a refund. Even though I hopped on the customer service chat as soon as I knew we may be late and they said the guide will be waiting at the meeting point, but they were not there. Then they sent us a pin to meet the guide, but it was located in the area only accessible with a ticket, and the guide had the ticket. Very disappointing! We purchased our own tickets for Versailles and used the audio tour and spent a lot less. Later a call to customer service was a waste of time only offering a future tour credit for only 25% of what I paid. Asked for a supervisor which they refused due to their "policy". I will not use this company again.

title: AVOID !
text: AVOID ! AVOID ! AVOID ! The most horrifying experience.  I booked my M J musical at QPAC via them.  My husband and I were planning to take our 2 younger daughters to see the show as birthday present.  I booked tickets with them as they appeared as Brisbane time and was the first website showed up in the search bar.  Not realizing that they were a third party from UK.  Anyway, go there showed QPAC my booking and then was told that my tickets were canceled.  The most embarrassing and terrible experience for my girls.  The show was sold out so we were devastated.  I still got charged by Headout and after numerous phone calls and online chat. I am still waiting for my refund.  They kept on saying that a manger will call me within 20 minutes but nobody ever called.  I was promised of  refund within 24 hours and it has now been 72 hours and more.  Still no email, no reply on refund.  Frustrated and do not know what else to do.  Maybe call up my bank to pose  a fraudulent transaction ?

title: Need better clarity in initial email around meeting place
text: They had two different meeting points in the same email for our time at Topkapi Palace in Istanbul. Very confusing around downloading the audio guide in advance and bringing passports, neither of which were actually needed. Confusion getting enough radio headsets which delayed the tour by at least 20 mins.

title: Granada hop on hop off train tour.
text:
Granada hop on hop off train tour.
I booked 3 tickets for this on 1/5/26 Booking ID: 31378661, the whole experience was shambolic and uncomfortable. The whole point of taking this tour was so my elderly father could see the sights of Granada as his walking is not good. We waited at no.8 on the tour for around 30 minutes, a train came but was full so we waited a further 40 minutes for the next one and were herded in like cattle by a very unhappy man. We had hoped to get off at the Alhambra but seeing the queues of people waiting to get on the already full train we just stayed on for fear of being stranded and missing our return train back to Antequera.

title: I had a very disappointing experience…
text:
I had a very disappointing experience with this company.

I booked a tour with hotel pickup included, and I was clearly told that I would be picked up from my hotel. However, no one showed up. There was no phone call, no email, no message — absolutely zero communication from their side.

I was left waiting and trying to figure out what was going on, but there was no way to reach them in time. As a result, I completely missed the tour.

I traveled all the way to New Zealand for this experience, and it was a total waste because of their lack of organization and communication. This is unacceptable for a tour provider.

If you value your time and money, I strongly recommend booking with a different company. This level of service is simply not reliable.

title: No refund
text:

Back home we asked Headout for a refund, because the service they sold to us did not happen. Their answer : "This might not the answer you were hoping for, but we don't do refunds."
I'll never use that service again, complete scam.

title: Auschwitz Tour
text:
I purchased what was advertised as a 7 hour guided tour of Auschwitz I and Auschwitz II-Birkenau with roundtrip transfer from Krakow, including entry tickets and an English guided tour inside both camps. This was a major reason I extended my trip to Poland, specifically to experience and bear witness to these historic sites properly.

The morning of the tour, my pickup location and time were abruptly changed with little notice. After arriving at Auschwitz I, our guide walked us around the outside of the museum entrance and into an area near the staff entry point where he provided historical information while pointing at things from a distance. Members of the group became confused and asked when we would be entering the museum. Only then were we informed that we did not actually have tickets for entry and would instead be viewing the camps from the sidewalk and exterior only.

At that point we were already 1.5 hours from Krakow with no alternative options. We paid for entry and a guided tour inside both camps and that is absolutely not what was delivered. This was false advertising at best and felt outright fraudulent.

The same thing happened at Auschwitz II-Birkenau. We viewed the camp from outside the fences and barbed wire rather than entering as advertised. Altogether, we spent roughly one hour actually “touring” while spending far longer on the transfer bus than at the sites themselves.

To make matters worse, halfway through the ride back we stopped at a gas station where I was unexpectedly told to get out and transfer into a random taxi while the rest of the group continued on to the salt mines. I then had to personally pay the taxi driver to get back to the original pickup point.

The entire experience was disorganized, misleading, and deeply disappointing given the significance of these memorial sites. I contacted the company immediately while still onsite seeking clarification and assistance and received no meaningful help. It has now been three days with no response whatsoever.

I will never book with this company again and strongly caution others to verify exactly what is included before purchasing.

title: Headout - Head Back!! Very Disappointing
text: Booked Blue Mosque and Bosphorus cruise for 2 in Istanbul. The Blue mosque was ok - guide was good but the “tour” lasted about 20 mins at most & the actual entry is free!! There were no tickets given for the cruise and after wasting 3 hours trying to locate the boat operator & failed calls to the helpline we had to purchase tickets for the cruise.. Very disappointing and a waste of money. AVOID!
